citations_verified_live_this_session_ncb.role: P50=26.6 mmHg / SaO2 96-98% reused from sibling MECHANISM_BLOOD_OXYGEN_TRANSPORT.md, re-verified self-consistent

citations_verified_live_this_session_ncb.title: West et al. 1983 Barometric pressures at extreme altitudes on Mt. Everest
citations_verified_live_this_session_ncb.role: PRIMARY: measured PB=253.0 Torr(n=1) summit, 283.6+-1.5(n=6) 8050m, 351.0+-1.0(n=16) 6300m, 400.4+-2.7(n=35) 5400m; all 'considerably higher' than ICAO Standard Atmosphere

citations_verified_live_this_session_ncb.title: West 1999 Barometric pressures on Mt Everest: new data
citations_verified_live_this_session_ncb.role: PRIMARY: confirms 253 Torr (1981) within ~1 Torr (1997); South Col 1998 (7986m) 284-287 Torr; regression PB=exp(6.63268-0.1112h-0.00149h^2), h in km; typical climbing-day summit 251-253 Torr

citations_verified_live_this_session_ncb.title: Grocott et al. 2009 NEJM Arterial blood gases in climbers on Everest (Caudwell Xtreme Everest)
citations_verified_live_this_session_ncb.role: PRIMARY: direct ABG sampling in 10 climbers; at 8400m (PB=272 measured) PaO2=24.6(19.1-29.5) mmHg, PaCO2=13.3(10.3-15.7), A-a=5.4; CaO2 maintained >=sea-level via Hb rise until 7100m, then 26% lower at 8400 vs 7100m

citations_verified_live_this_session_ncb.title: West et al. 1983 Maximal exercise at extreme altitudes on Everest (AMREE)
citations_verified_live_this_session_ncb.role: PRIMARY: PIO2 43 Torr chamber = summit-equivalent; direct summit alveolar sample PACO2=7-8 Torr (also reproduced in a subject at 6300m/14%O2); ventilation exceeded 200 L/min at 6300m air-breathing

citations_verified_live_this_session_ncb.title: Sutton et al. 1988 Operation Everest II: oxygen transport during exercise at extreme simulated altitude
citations_verified_live_this_session_ncb.role: PRIMARY: 8 men, 40-day chamber ascent, direct arterial+mixed-venous catheter sampling at PIO2=80/63/49/43 Torr; VO2max 3.98+-0.20->1.17+-0.08 L/min; at PIO2=43/60W: PaO2=28+-1, PaCO2=11+-1, PvO2=14.8+-1; 'most important adaptation' = 4x rise in alveolar ventilation; diffusion+circulatory transport largely unaffected

citations_verified_live_this_session_ncb.title: Lenfant et al. 1968 JCI Effect of altitude on O2 binding by hemoglobin and organic phosphate
citations_verified_live_this_session_ncb.role: PRIMARY: within 24h of altitude change, Hb-O2 affinity AND red-cell organic phosphate (2,3-DPG) both shift in parallel -- 'rapid adaptive mechanism', right-shift aiding tissue O2 unloading

citations_verified_live_this_session_ncb.title: Weil et al. 1970 JCI Hypoxic ventilatory drive in normal man
citations_verified_live_this_session_ncb.role: PRIMARY: VE adjustment to PAO2 change complete in 18-23 sec; hyperbolic VE-PAO2 curve

citations_verified_live_this_session_ncb.title: Easton, Slykerman, Anthonisen 1986 Ventilatory response to sustained hypoxia
citations_verified_live_this_session_ncb.role: PRIMARY: biphasic HVR -- brisk rise then decline to an intermediate plateau over 25 min, stable to 1h

citations_verified_live_this_session_ncb.title: Eckardt et al. 1989 Rate of EPO formation in response to acute hypobaric hypoxia
citations_verified_live_this_session_ncb.role: PRIMARY: EPO significantly elevated after 84 min(4000m)/114 min(3000m); 1.8x/3.0x rise over 5.5h; post-hypoxia EPO half-life 5.2h (matches erythropoiesis doc's own disclosed ~5-6h assumption)

citations_verified_live_this_session_ncb.title: Dempsey et al. 1979 JCI CSF [H+] in ventilatory deacclimatization
citations_verified_live_this_session_ncb.role: PRIMARY: hyperventilation persists ~1h post-return-to-normoxia (CSF pH still normal/alkaline), then falls over 1-13h as CSF re-acidifies -- the reverse/washout transient, corroborating an hours-scale mechanism

citations_verified_live_this_session_ncb.title: Bird et al. 2021 Time course of ventilatory and renal acid-base acclimatization
citations_verified_live_this_session_ncb.role: PRIMARY: n=16 direct radial arterial samples, rapid ascent to 3800m; pHa compensated within 24h, PaCO2/HCO3- both already lower by day 2

citations_verified_live_this_session_ncb.title: Zouboules et al. 2018 Renal reactivity: acid-base compensation during incremental ascent
citations_verified_live_this_session_ncb.role: PRIMARY: n direct arterial samples during 10-day incremental ascent to 5160m (Nepal); renal reactivity increases and plateaus after 5 days, unchanged at higher subsequent altitudes

citations_verified_live_this_session_ncb.title: Bartsch & Saltin 2008 General introduction to altitude adaptation
citations_verified_live_this_session_ncb.role: REVIEW: plasma volume -24-48h; CaO2 'normalized' by 4+ weeks; peak VO2 after long acclimatization 'essentially unaltered' vs acute; AMS 10-30% at 2500-3000m; edema thresholds; ascent-rate guidance 300 m/day >2000m

citations_verified_live_this_session_ncb.title: Maggiorini et al. 1990 BMJ Prevalence of AMS in the Swiss Alps
citations_verified_live_this_session_ncb.role: PRIMARY: n=466 climbers, 4 huts; AMS prevalence 9%/13%/34%/53% at 2850/3050/3650/4559m, strictly altitude-dependent

citations_verified_live_this_session_ncb.title: Hackett, Rennie, Levine 1976 Lancet Incidence/importance/prophylaxis of AMS
citations_verified_live_this_session_ncb.role: PRIMARY: n=278 hikers, 4243m Pheriche; overall AMS 53%; severity 'highly correlated with speed of ascent'; 12 severe (7 HAPE+5 HACE) cases, 11/12 had flown in, 9/12 only 1 night before symptoms

citations_verified_live_this_session_ncb.title: Villafuerte & Corante 2016 Chronic Mountain Sickness: clinical aspects
citations_verified_live_this_session_ncb.role: REVIEW: CMS = severe symptomatic excessive erythrocytosis, Hb>=19 g/dL (F) / >=21 g/dL (M), with accentuated hypoxemia

citations_verified_live_this_session_ncb.title: Leon-Velarde et al. 2005 Consensus statement on chronic/subacute high altitude disease
citations_verified_live_this_session_ncb.role: topical/provenance: international consensus framework for CMS diagnosis/management

citations_verified_live_this_session_ncb.title: Roach et al. 2018 The 2018 Lake Louise AMS Score
citations_verified_live_this_session_ncb.role: PRIMARY (methodological): revises 1991 score, removes disturbed-sleep item (more altitude-hypoxia-per-se than AMS-specific)

citations_verified_live_this_session_ncb.title: Wehrlin & Hallen 2006 Linear decrease in VO2max and performance with altitude
citations_verified_live_this_session_ncb.role: PRIMARY: 8 endurance athletes, hypobaric chamber 300-2800m; VO2max declines 6.3%/1000m (4.6-7.5% range) linear; 66+-1.6->55+-1.6 mL/kg/min; SpO2(exhaustion) 89.0+-2.9%->76.5+-4.0%

citations_verified_live_this_session_ncb.title: Levine & Stray-Gundersen 1997 Living high-training low
citations_verified_live_this_session_ncb.role: PRIMARY: n=39 runners; VO2max +5% (both altitude groups, tracks +9% red cell mass, r=0.37); 5km time improved 13.4+-10s in HIGH-LOW group ONLY (r=0.65 vs VO2max change)
